summary: A travel-style guide to six street art festivals scheduled for late 2023 across Europe, Australia, North America, Asia, Africa and South America. It describes each festival's location, dates, curator or director, and activities such as tours, workshops, and live painting. It frames street art as an evolving, celebrated form that connects communities and cultures.
one_line: Guide to six 2023 street art festivals worldwide, from Lisbon to Bogotá, with dates, organizers, locations and activities.
key_facts: MURAL Festival takes place in Lisbon, Portugal, on 14th-23rd October 2023, curated by street artist Hugo Cantagalo, in the Alfama and Mouraria neighborhoods.
MURAL Festival offers guided tours, workshops, and live performances.
Wonderwalls Festival is held in Wollongong, Australia, from 3rd to 12th November 2023, curated by street artist Rone.
Wonderwalls features street-art walks, art battles, mural bike tours, and outdoor film screenings alongside large-scale murals.
POW! WOW! Worldwide is a global network of festivals that began in Hawaii; POW! WOW! Long Beach, California runs 1st-10th September 2023 under director Jasper Wong.
POW! WOW! Long Beach organizes school programs, gallery shows, and talks.
HKwalls runs in Hong Kong from 20th to 29th November 2023, centered in the Sham Shui Po district, with director Maria Wong.
HKwalls includes live murals, music sessions, and artist dialogues, and aims to educate the public about street art.
FestiWall takes place in Rabat, Morocco, from 15th to 24th September 2023, organized by Yassine Hattab, with themes of identity, social justice, and communal unity.
FestiWall includes youth-centered workshops and panel discussions.
The Graffiti Art Festival is held in Bogotá, Colombia, from 5th to 14th December 2023, spearheaded by Diego García, in the La Candelaria district.
The Graffiti Art Festival provides a platform for emerging artists while honoring veterans of street art.
